section_summary: This section contains the concluding portion of a Japanese government study examining the demographic history, post-World War II repatriation, and legal status of Japanese and native populations in Formosa, Kwangtung Leased Territory, Saghalien, and the Kurile Islands. It also includes an August 1949 State Department circular letter from Niles W. Bond transmitting Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs procedures for Japanese nationals abroad to communicate directly with their government regarding nationality and personal status, addressed to various Japanese-American newspapers. Finally, the section includes diplomatic memoranda from the embassies of Venezuela and Colombia acknowledging receipt of these communication procedures.

subfiles.about: A statistical and historical study of Japanese and indigenous populations, post-World War II repatriation, and legal and property status in Formosa, Kwangtung Leased Territory, Saghalien, and the Kurile Islands.
subfiles.summary: This concluding section of a Japanese government study surveys demographic trends, post-World War II repatriation, and legal status across Formosa, Kwangtung Leased Territory, Saghalien, and the Kurile Islands. It details the repatriation of civilians, the retention of indispensable technicians, Chinese nationality decrees for Formosans, and SCAP jurisdictional rulings. Furthermore, it highlights the harsh detention of Japanese laborers under Soviet occupation in Saghalien and the Kuriles, citing historical treaties regarding residency and property rights.
subfiles.title: Study on Japanese Overseas Territories: Formosa, Kwangtung Leased Territory, Saghalien, and the Kurile Islands

subfiles.about: A State Department circular letter notifying Japanese-American newspapers that Japanese nationals abroad may communicate directly with the Japanese Government regarding nationality and personal status, enclosing an explanatory memorandum.
subfiles.from: Niles W. Bond, Acting Chief, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Acting Chief Niles W. Bond of the Division of Northeast Asian Affairs transmits identical circular letters to Japanese-American newspapers across the United States and Hawaii, including the Rafu Shimpo, Hokubei Mainichi, Hawaii Herald, and Hawaii Times. The letter explains that the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers has authorized Japanese nationals and former nationals residing abroad to communicate directly with the Japanese Government on nationality and personal status issues. Bond encloses an explanatory memorandum from the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs and requests that editors publicize these procedures.
subfiles.title: Circular Letter to Japanese-American Newspapers Regarding Communication on Nationality and Personal Status
subfiles.to: Japanese-American Newspapers (Rafu Shimpo, Hokubei Mainichi, Hawaii Herald, Hawaii Times, and others)

subfiles.about: The Venezuelan Ambassador acknowledges receipt of a State Department memorandum concerning communication procedures for Japanese nationals on nationality and personal status.
subfiles.from: José Rafael Pocaterra, Ambassador of Venezuela
subfiles.summary: Ambassador José Rafael Pocaterra acknowledges the State Department's August 22 memorandum and notes that Japanese nationality communication procedures have been transmitted to Venezuela.
subfiles.title: Note No. 1769 from the Embassy of Venezuela Acknowledging Nationality Procedures Memorandum

subfiles.about: The Colombian Embassy acknowledges receipt of the State Department's August 22 memorandum and report regarding communication procedures for Japanese nationals.
subfiles.summary: The Colombian Embassy acknowledges the State Department's August 22 memorandum and confirms forwarding Japanese nationality procedures to the Colombian Government.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from the Embassy of Colombia Acknowledging Nationality Procedures Memorandum
